entries.topic: Debate, criticism and later genocide statement
entries.context: JTA’s January 12 report links his debate refusal (while both opponents answered yes), audience jeers and ongoing criticism to his later Sunday January 11 video saying genocide. This guide treats that timing as a political-pressure concern. Preserve that sequence rather than describing an unqualified positive ideological shift. Opportunistic motive is an interpretation, not an independently established fact.

entries.topic: Appropriations votes, explanation and UNRWA support
entries.context: Keep these together: January 14 Yea on H.R.7006; January 16 explanation that Republicans “snuck” provisions into the bill and his claim of prior UNRWA-funding votes; February 3 Nay on the later H.R.7148 package; and his separate March 27, 2025 UNRWA-restoration cosponsorship. The later No does not erase the initial Yes. His explanation does not prove he was unaware; the post’s claimed prior UNRWA vote is not independently identified as a specific roll call here. Cosponsorship is not a vote.

entries.topic: Dated primary cosponsorship supersedes undated guide prose
entries.context: Official bill-status XML lists H.R.3565 cosponsorship from July 14, 2026. The old Vote for Peace no-Block-the-Bombs note was retired as obsolete through source review. Keep the separate current Ally rating; do not describe present opposition or an unresolved sponsorship conflict from that old note.

action_groups.context: Consider the entire sequence, including separate restoration support. These are different packages and a cosponsorship, not interchangeable votes. Preserve source assessments and any candidate-specific explanation; do not infer a reason for changed responses from the sequence alone.
